assumptions: Planar2R model with massless links, point mass m1 at the elbow and m2 at the second tip; θ1 measured upward from horizontal, θ2 relative, gravity downward. No friction or extra loads. solution.justification: The nonzero cosine retains every expanded Vx coefficient. The task force uses the derivative of rotating velocity components, and Jᵀ maps that force back to the same joint effort as Mqddot+V+G.

optionExplanations.o1: All transformed terms, the component-derivative correction and the transpose effort map are included.
optionExplanations.o2: This uses J⁻ᵀV without subtracting Mx Jdot qdot; both its velocity force and recovered efforts are wrong.
optionExplanations.o3: This drops the cosθ2-dependent contributions from Vx1: the missing terms total43/6 N at these parameters.
optionExplanations.o4: The task dynamics is correct, but the final effort uses JF instead of JᵀF.

steps: Check directly: Mqddot+V+G gives the same τ.

formulas.expression: a_c=J qddot+Jdot qdot; Mx=J⁻ᵀMJ⁻¹; Vx=J⁻ᵀ(V−MJ⁻¹Jdot qdot); Gx=J⁻ᵀG; F=Mx a_c+Vx+Gx; τ=JᵀF

variables.a_c: time derivative of tool-frame velocity components
variables.Jdot: time derivative of the same Jacobian components

assumptions: Planar2R model with massless links, point mass m1 at the elbow and m2 at the second tip; θ1 measured upward from horizontal, θ2 relative, gravity downward. No friction or extra loads. All task vectors use the displayed rotating tool axes; a_c=d(v_T)/dt is the derivative of velocity components, not inertial acceleration components.
J is nonsingular; radians are dimensionless in the mechanics identities.

solution.simpleExplanation: The nonzero cosine retains every expanded Vx coefficient. The task force uses the derivative of rotating velocity components, and Jᵀ maps that force back to the same joint effort as Mqddot+V+G.
misconceptions: This uses J⁻ᵀV without subtracting Mx Jdot qdot; both its velocity force and recovered efforts are wrong.
This drops the cosθ2-dependent contributions from Vx1: the missing terms total43/6 N at these parameters.
The task dynamics is correct, but the final effort uses JF instead of JᵀF.
examTraps: Do not discard the cosine-dependent Vx coefficients just because an earlier worked state used θ2=90°.
Do not equate a_c with inertial acceleration in rotating axes.
Transform task effort with Jᵀ, not J.
